chapter.title_en: The Lantern by the Plum Tree
chapter.summary: On the first night after Grandma's funeral, Mia cannot understand where her grandmother has gone, and her mother answers honestly and gently instead of explaining the ache away. Together they fill the old brass lantern, carry it out into the rain, and hang it on a low branch beside Nubi's plum tree hollow — finally giving the owl a light of her own. Mia learns that missing someone is love with nowhere to go, and that she can miss Grandma terribly and still be warm, safe, and okay.

pages.en: The house was very quiet that night. Too quiet, Mia thought. The rain tapped the roof the way it always had, but Grandma's slippers sat by the door with nobody in them. Mia sat on the edge of her bed, holding Nubi's speckled feather so tightly that her fingers went pink. Mum came in, sat down beside her, and did not say anything at all for a little while.
pages.ko: 그날 밤, 집 안은 아주 조용했어요. 미아는 생각했어요. 너무너무 조용하다고요. 지붕 위로 빗방울은 늘 하던 대로 톡톡 떨어지는데, 문 앞 할머니 슬리퍼에는 아무도 없었어요. 미아는 침대 끝에 앉아 누비의 깃털을 손가락이 발개지도록 꼭 쥐었어요. 엄마가 들어와 옆에 앉았고, 한참 동안 아무 말도 하지 않았어요.
pages.scene: A small dim bedroom at night, rain streaking the dark window. Mia sits on the edge of her bed clutching a speckled owl feather; her mother sits beside her in silence. An empty pair of slippers by the door.
pages.wardrobe: Soft cotton pyjamas with tiny star print; bare feet. Mum in a grey cardigan over pyjamas.

pages.en: "Where did Grandma go?" Mia asked. Mum took a slow breath. "Grandma died, my love. Her body got very old and very tired, and it stopped. She isn't hurting anywhere. But she won't come back." Mia pressed her hand flat against her chest. "Then why does it hurt right here?" she whispered.
pages.ko: "할머니는 어디로 간 거예요?" 미아가 물었어요. 엄마는 천천히 숨을 쉬었어요. "할머니는 돌아가셨어. 몸이 아주 오래 살아서 많이 지쳤고, 그래서 멈춘 거야. 이제 아프지 않으셔. 하지만 다시 오시지는 않아." 미아는 손바닥을 가슴에 꾹 댔어요. "그런데 왜 여기가 아파요?" 미아가 작게 물었어요.
pages.scene: Close on Mia's face, brows knitted, one hand flat on her chest. Mum leaning in, eyes kind and a little wet, hand resting on the quilt.
pages.wardrobe: Same star-print pyjamas; Mum in grey cardigan.

pages.en: "Because that's where all your love for her is," said Mum. "When someone goes away, the love doesn't go with them. It stays. And love with nowhere to go feels heavy, like a full cup you can't put down. That heavy feeling has a name. It's called missing someone." Mia thought about that. Then, tap-tap, something small knocked on the window glass.
pages.ko: "거기에 할머니를 사랑하는 마음이 가득 들어 있어서 그래." 엄마가 말했어요. "누가 떠나도 사랑은 따라가지 않아. 그대로 남아 있어. 갈 곳을 못 찾은 사랑은 무거워. 가득 찬 컵을 계속 들고 있는 것처럼 말이야. 그 무거운 마음에도 이름이 있단다. 그리움이라고 해." 미아가 가만히 생각하는데, 톡톡, 창문에 무언가 작게 부딪혔어요.
pages.scene: Mum speaking softly, cupping her hands as if holding an invisible full cup. Behind them, a round owl silhouette appears at the rainy window.
pages.wardrobe: Star-print pyjamas; Mum in grey cardigan.

pages.en: It was Nubi, round and rain-speckled, her amber eyes blinking through the water. She looked at the brass lantern on the sill, cold and dark, the way she always used to when Grandma was here. "She's waiting," said Mia. And all at once Mia knew exactly what she wanted to do — the thing she had been planning since the night of the plum tree.
pages.ko: 누비였어요. 동글동글하고 빗방울이 송송 맺힌 누비가 호박색 눈을 깜빡였어요. 누비는 창턱 위에 차갑게 식어 있는 놋쇠 등불을 바라보았어요. 할머니가 계실 때 늘 그랬던 것처럼요. "누비가 기다리고 있어요." 미아가 말했어요. 그 순간, 미아는 자기가 무얼 하고 싶은지 딱 알았어요. 자두나무에 갔던 그날 밤부터 마음에 품고 있던 그 일이요.
pages.scene: Nubi the small owl perched on the outside sill, wet and round, amber eyes glowing. Inside, the dark brass lantern on the windowsill. Mia's face lifting with quiet purpose.

pages.en: They fetched the dented tin from the kitchen cupboard and filled the lantern together. "Now we wait," Mia said, just like Grandma used to. "The wick has to drink slowly." So they sat on the kitchen floor and waited, and the waiting felt a little bit like missing — quiet, and long, and not empty at all.
pages.ko: 둘은 부엌 찬장에서 찌그러진 기름통을 꺼내 등불에 기름을 채웠어요. "이제 기다려야 해요." 미아가 말했어요. 할머니가 늘 하시던 말처럼요. "심지가 천천히 기름을 마셔야 하거든요." 그래서 둘은 부엌 바닥에 앉아 기다렸어요. 기다리는 마음은 그리운 마음이랑 조금 닮아 있었어요. 조용하고, 길고, 하나도 텅 비지 않았어요.
pages.scene: Warm kitchen at night, Mia and Mum sitting on the floor beside the brass lantern and the small dented oil tin, waiting patiently. Rain on the dark kitchen window.

pages.en: Then out into the drizzle they went, boots on, umbrella up, all the way to the old plum tree. Mia hooked the lantern on the low branch right beside Nubi's hollow — a light of her very own, at last. The wick caught. A small gold flame stood up in the rain and did not blow out. Nubi swooped down, settled at her doorway, and blinked slowly, once, like a thank you.
pages.ko: 둘은 장화를 신고 우산을 쓰고 보슬비 속으로 나갔어요. 정원 끝, 오래된 자두나무까지요. 미아는 누비의 나무 구멍 바로 옆 낮은 가지에 등불을 걸었어요. 드디어 누비만의 등불이 생긴 거예요. 심지에 불이 붙었어요. 작고 노란 불꽃이 빗속에서 똑바로 서서, 꺼지지 않았어요. 누비가 내려와 제 집 앞에 앉더니 천천히 한 번 눈을 깜빡였어요. 꼭 고맙다고 인사하는 것처럼요.
pages.scene: Night garden in soft drizzle. Mia on tiptoe hanging the lit brass lantern on a low branch beside the plum tree hollow; Mum holding the umbrella over her. Nubi settling in the glowing hollow.
pages.wardrobe: Yellow raincoat over pyjamas, red rubber boots; Mum in a long dark raincoat holding a wide umbrella.

pages.en: Standing in the golden circle of light, Mia said it out loud: "Grandma, I miss you." And then she cried, with the rain on her hood and Mum's arms around her. The lantern kept burning the whole time. Crying did not put it out.
pages.ko: 동그란 금빛 불빛 안에 서서, 미아는 소리 내어 말했어요. "할머니, 보고 싶어요." 그리고 울었어요. 모자 위로 빗방울이 떨어지고, 엄마가 미아를 폭 안아 주었어요. 그동안에도 등불은 계속 타올랐어요. 우는 걸로는 불이 꺼지지 않았어요.
pages.scene: Mia crying in her mother's arms under the umbrella, both lit warm gold by the hanging lantern. Nubi watching quietly from the hollow. Rain shining in the light.
pages.wardrobe: Yellow raincoat, red boots; Mum in dark raincoat.

pages.en: Back inside, dry socks, warm bed, the feather tucked under her pillow. "Will it always hurt this much?" Mia asked. "It gets softer," Mum said. "And you'll still miss her. Missing her just means you loved her — that part never has to stop." Mia turned toward the window. Far down the garden, one small light glowed steadily in the rain. She missed Grandma very much. And she was warm, and safe, and okay. She fell asleep just like that.
pages.ko: 집에 돌아와 마른 양말을 신고, 따뜻한 이불 속으로 들어갔어요. 깃털은 베개 밑에 살짝 넣어 두었고요. "이 마음이 계속 이렇게 아플까요?" 미아가 물었어요. "조금씩 부드러워질 거야." 엄마가 말했어요. "그래도 할머니가 보고 싶긴 할 거야. 보고 싶다는 건 많이 사랑했다는 뜻이거든. 그건 멈추지 않아도 돼." 미아는 창밖을 보았어요. 정원 저 끝에서 작은 불빛 하나가 빗속에서 조용히 빛나고 있었어요. 할머니가 아주 많이 보고 싶었어요. 그리고 미아는 따뜻하고, 안전하고, 괜찮았어요. 그렇게 스르르 잠이 들었어요.
pages.scene: Mia tucked into bed, sleepy, cheek on pillow, feather peeking out beneath it. Through the window, far down the dark garden, a tiny warm lantern glow by the plum tree. Mum sitting at the bedside.
pages.wardrobe: Fresh dry pyjamas (soft blue), thick socks; Mum in grey cardigan.

new_characters.name: Mum
new_characters.traits: Honest and gentle; answers hard questions plainly without hurrying a feeling away; grieving too, and unashamed of it.

new_world.name: The lantern by the plum tree
new_world.description: The old brass lantern, now hung on a low branch beside Nubi's hollow at the end of the garden, where it burns on rainy nights as the owl's own outdoor light and as a small keeping-place for Mia's love for Grandma.

threads_opened.summary: Mia wants to collect and remember all of Grandma's small everyday sayings and know-how (like how the wick must drink slowly), so none of them are lost.
Mia must learn to fill and light the lantern by herself now, without Grandma's hands to guide hers.

threads_resolved.how: On the first night after the funeral, Mia and Mum fill the brass lantern with oil and hang it on the low branch beside Nubi's hollow in the plum tree, giving the owl the outdoor light Mia had promised her.

concerns.issue: The child helps fill an oil lantern from a tin of fuel; a young listener could see this as an activity to copy. It is fully supervised by the parent throughout, and no matches or burns are shown, so it stays a low-level note rather than a real hazard.

Going outside into the rain at night to hang a lit lantern on a tree. Mitigated by the fact that the child is with her mother the whole time (boots, umbrella, returns straight indoors), so it does not model wandering off alone.

Death is stated plainly ('Grandma died... her body stopped... she won't come back'). This is direct, but it is age-appropriate honesty, immediately followed by reassurance that she is not hurting and by the mother's comforting explanation of grief on the following pages. This is the app working as intended.

recent_chapters.summary: The night before her vaccination, Mia is silent with fear until Grandma invites her to carry the newly lit brass lantern outdoors for the first time. Following Nubi through the drizzle, they find the owl's real home in a hollow of the old plum tree, and Mia finally says out loud that she is frightened. At the clinic the next morning she cries — and goes anyway, learning that tears and bravery can share one small heart.

A loud thunderstorm wakes Mia in the night and she hides under her quilt, refusing to come out. Grandma sits beside her without pulling the quilt away, and the old brass lantern — its wick having drunk oil all night — finally lights, revealing Nubi sheltering under the eaves. Mia learns to count the space between flash and rumble and discovers that the storm, like every scary thing, moves on and passes.

On a rainy evening after supper, Mia tries again to make the old brass lantern light, and Grandma shows her that the dry wick must slowly drink its oil before any flame can come. While they wait, Grandma reveals that the lantern was made for her when she was a small, frightened girl, and Nubi the owl returns to wait at the window beside Mia until bedtime.

On a rainy evening, Mia discovers an old brass lantern in her grandmother's attic, but no matter what she tries, it will not light. She must go to bed in the dark anyway, and with her grandmother's words and a small owl named Nubi at the window, she learns that being scared and being brave can live in the same heart.

open_threads.summary: Mia wants to hang a small light of her own by the plum tree so Nubi has a lantern outside her hollow on dark nights.

characters.name: Mia
characters.traits: Curious, tender-hearted, loves owls and rain; scared of the dark but willing to stay with the feeling.

characters.name: Grandma
characters.role: Mia's grandmother, keeper of the old house
characters.traits: Warm, unhurried, never dismisses a feeling; gives simple wise answers.

characters.name: Nubi
characters.role: small owl who appears at Mia's rainy window
characters.traits: Round, rain-speckled, amber-eyed, polite and quietly loyal.

world.name: Grandma's attic
world.description: A dusty attic above Grandma's house, smelling of old blankets and rain, opened with a small silver key.

world.name: The brass lantern
world.description: An old brass lantern with round glass and a hand-worn handle that refuses to light; tiny scratched words on its base read 'For the one who is scared and goes anyway.'

world.name: The silver key
world.description: Grandma's small silver key that opens the attic door.

world.name: The tin of lamp oil
world.description: Grandma's small dented tin of lamp oil, kept in the kitchen cupboard; the lantern's dry wick must drink from it slowly before it can ever burn.

world.name: The eaves of Grandma's house
world.description: The sheltered overhang just outside Mia's bedroom window, where Nubi tucks herself out of the rain during storms.

world.name: The plum tree hollow
world.description: A round hollow low in the trunk of the old plum tree at the end of Grandma's garden, lined with dry leaves — this is where Nubi actually lives and sleeps.

world.name: Nubi's speckled feather
world.description: A small rain-speckled feather Mia found at the foot of the plum tree; she carries it in her pocket for courage and keeps it under her pillow.
